A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same I2EvDet/EvRT-DETR work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gen1 and 1Mpx detection results, multiple ablations, and YOLOX baseline experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and additionally reports temporally adapted YOLOX results, detailed evaluation metrics, and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The RT-DETR adaptation procedure and equations (1)–(4) remain unchanged. v3 adds an EvYOLOX instantiation, inserting residual ConvLSTM modules between the frozen YOLOX PAFPN neck and detection head (Appendix A.4), extending the framework to another architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gen1 and 1Mpx/Gen4 automotive object detection with the same represented classes and domains. The added architecture experiments and qualitative examples use this existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains every external comparator. Frame-based YOLOX baselines already appeared in v2; v3 expands their comparison with EvYOLOX-T/S/L/X and EvRT-DETR-B in Table 9. Appendix A.5 also introduces an experimentally evaluated end-to-end training control.

E3.justification: v3 expands evaluation to recall at multiple IoU thresholds (Table 12) and reports a joint versus two-stage training comparison (Appendix A.5). Retained experiments keep their stated splits, preprocessing, and training budgets. Newly specified timing boundaries and YOLOX inference thresholds are disclosures, not established changes to existing settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D add a direct test of temporal adaptation across four YOLOX variants, substantially extending validation of framework generalizability beyond v2's frame-only architecture comparison. Appendix A.5 adds training-strategy observations, and Figures 5–6 add comparisons against ground truth. Existing ablations remain, including the kernel-size study moved from Table 2 to Table 8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or comparable uncertainty estimates. v3's qualitative training-stability statement and additional mean recall metrics do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged. Substantial additions include EvYOLOX-T/S/L/X Gen1 mAP values of 42.4/43.6/46.6/47.8, further precision and recall metrics, and qualitative training findings. New reporting inconsistencies include Table 12's RT-DETR-B Gen1 mAP of 47.5 versus Table 1's 47.6, and 1Mpx mAR75 exceeding mAR50. Appendix D states YOLOX gains of 4.4–6.4, although Table 9 implies 3.5–6.6.

T1.justification: The event-histogram expression and temporal-adaptation equations are unchanged. v3 explains existing event symbols and the Kronecker delta, without introducing new mathematical reasoning, formal assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same adaptation-framework contribution, generality claim, and state-of-the-art margins of 2.3 mAP on Gen1 and 1.4 on 1Mpx. The YOLOX experiments provide new support for an existing claim.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 specifies applicability to detectors with separable feature extraction and detection components, while removing the representation-collapse and module-deactivation rationale. Appendix A.5 adds a practical training rationale qualified by limited hyperparameter exploration. Appendix D emphasizes cross-architecture applicability, and Figure 6 acknowledges remaining difficulties with heavy occlusion.

D1.justification: Appendices A.3–A.4 add YOLOX implementation provenance, a code commit, adapter placement and configuration, and NMS/confidence thresholds of 0.65/0.01. Section 4.1 newly explains runtime accounting, including differing preprocessing inclusion among comparisons. Existing RT-DETR hardware, budgets, and project code access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to the YOLOX implementation and Path Aggregation Network. Existing research positioning is largely retained; most other bibliography edits update metadata or publication versions of already cited works.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits prose throughout, simplifies Section 3.2, adds a generalizability subsection, and reorganizes the appendices. The principal narrative and most paragraphs remain recognizable, making this a focused revision rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures 5–6 with ground-truth comparisons, introduces Tables 2 and 12, and expands the YOLOX table. The kernel-size table moves to the appendix. Figures 1–4 and the principal benchmark display retain their content and overall design.

improvement.justification: The temporal YOLOX experiments directly test architecture generalizability, which v2's frame-only comparison did not establish. Added implementation details, training qualifications, and ground-truth examples improve reproducibility and interpretation. These gains strengthen support for the main framework, although inconsistencies in the new metrics table and the misstated YOLOX gain range limit the improvement.
